Received2APR2019
Accepted21JUN2019
Acceptedarticleonline1JUL2019 1. Introduction
Publishedonline8JUL2019
The South China Block (SCB) is considered as one of the continents that rifted off the margin of
Gondwana, drifted northward, and accreted onto the East Asian continent from the Paleozoic to
Mesozoic (Golonka et al., 2006; Metcalfe, 2013). Existing geologic, paleomagnetic, and paleontologic evi-
dence suggests the affinity of the SCB with East Gondwana during the Early Paleozoic (Burrett et al.,
1990,2014;Hanetal.,2015;Lietal.,2017;Nie,1991;Zhangetal.,2001,2015;Zhang,2004).Thepresence
ofwarm‐waterflorasandabsenceofglacialdepositsinCarboniferous–PermianstrataoftheSCBindicate
no relationship with Gondwana (Metcalfe, 2013). However, the SCB's position relative to Gondwana
duringtheEarlyPaleozoicremainshighlycontroversial,withtheSCBvariouslyassignedtotheproximity
ofNWIndia(Burrettetal.,2014;Li&Powell,2001),NEIndia–WAustralia(Cawoodetal.,2013,2018),
or NW Australia (Han et al., 2015; Yang et al., 2004; Zhang et al., 2001), or as an isolated block away
fromGondwanathroughouttheEarlyPaleozoicandEarlyDevonian(Cocks&Torsvik,2013).Themajor
cause of such uncertainty is the lack of robust paleomagnetic constraints on the position of the SCB
during the Devonian, which is a key transitional period for the evolution of the Paleo‐Tethys Ocean but
has the least reliable data from the SCB and globally (Torsvik et al., 2012). In this study, we report a
new paleopole that meets all seven criteria of Van der Voo (1990) from the Middle Devonian (Givetian)
redbedsinNWHunanProvince,China.Incombinationwithavailabledata,wepresentanewpaleogeo-
graphic evolution model for the connection and separation between the SCB and Gondwana
©2019.AmericanGeophysicalUnion.
AllRightsReserved. duringthePaleozoic.

2. Geological Setting andPaleomagnetic Sampling
PaleomagneticsampleswerecollectedfromtheZhangjiajieandBaojingregionsinNWHunanProvince,
SouthChina(Figure1a).Inthestudyarea,theDevonianstratadisconformablyoverlieUpper‐Siluriangreen
siltstoneandunderliePermiancarbonaterocks(Figures1b,1c,andS1).TheDevonianstrataconsistofthe
Middle Devonian Yuntaiguan Formation (YF) and Upper Devonian Huangjiadeng Formation (HF). The
YF'slowerpart,284to361mthick,ischaracterizedbyreddish,medium‐tothick‐beddedquartzsandstone
withthininterbedsofpurplesiltstoneandsiltyshale.Itsupperpart,69to242mthick,ismainlycomposedof
pink‐white, thick‐bedded quartz sandstone with minor purple‐gray siltstone interbeds. The YF's age is
assigned to the Givetian stage based on spore assemblages (Gao, 1989) and plant fossils (such as
Protolepidodendron scharyanum–Barrandeina dusliana, Protopteridium minutum, Lepidodendropsis sp.,
andPsilophytitessp.;Chen,1959;Zhuetal.,1983).TheHF,4to29mthick,ischaracterizedbyFe‐bearing
purple siltstone/mudstone or oolitic/pisolitic/brecciated hematite. Abundant plant fossils including
Leptophyloeum rhombicum and Cyclosligma kiliorkense found in the HF denote its Late Devonian age
(Hou et al., 1988). The Paleozoic strata were tilted due to the NW–SE compression of the Yanshanian
(LateJurassic–EarlyCretaceous)tectonicevent(Lietal.,2014;Liuetal.,2012),formingNNEtrendingfolds
withgentlebedding(Figures1band1c).

Atotalof400samplesof46siteswerecollectedfromfivesectionsoftheYF(Figures1andS1andS2inthe
supportinginformation).Amongthese,23siteswerearrangedcontinuouslycoveringan~370‐m‐thickinter-
valintheQishuwanSection,inwhichtheYFisupto600mthickandexposedcontinuouslyfromitsbottom
to top. The other 23 sites covered the other four sections (Baojing, Longzhai, Sangzhi, andTaozixi) with
differentbeddingattitudes.Mostofthesamplesarepurplesiltstone,andafewarequartzsandstone.Each
site contains 6–15 samples, spanning a stratigraphic thickness of 0.5–15 m. All the sample cores were
orientedwithamagneticcompassandSuncompasswhenpossible,andthedifferenceswerelessthan1°
betweenthetwomethods,whichindicatesinsignificantlocalmagneticanomaly.
3. Methods andResults
AnisotropyofmagneticsusceptibilitywasmeasuredfirstusinganAGICOMFK1kappa‐bridge.Afterthat,
remanentmagnetizationsweremeasuredona2G‐755Kthree‐axiscryogenicmagnetometer,andthermal
demagnetizationswereperformedonanMMTDSCfurnace,bothofwhichhaveinternalresidualfieldsof
lessthan10nT.Tofurthercharacterizethemagneticmineralogy,representativesampleswerechosenfor
isothermal remanent magnetization (IRM) acquisition curves, backfield demagnetizations of IRM, and
Lowrietest(Lowrie,1990).Remanentmagnetizationmeasurementsanddemagnetizationswereconducted
in a magnetically shielded room with a residual field of less than 300 nT in the Paleomagnetism and
EnvironmentalMagnetismLaboratoryatthe China UniversityofGeosciences,Beijing.Magneticcompo-
nentsweredeterminedusingprincipalcomponentanalysis(Kirschvink,1980)withmaximumangledevia-
tionlessthan15°,andmeandirectionswerecalculatedusingFisherstatistics(Fisher,1953).Paleomagnetic
datawereanalyzedusingthesoftwarepackagesofPaleoMag(Jones,2002),PaleoMac(Cogné,2003),and
PmagPy (Tauxe et al., 2016). Plate reconstructions were built using the open‐source software
GPlates(www.gplates.org).
Anisotropyofmagneticsusceptibilitymeasurementsrevealedanoblateanisotropyofmagneticsusceptibil-
ityellipsoid(shapeparameterT=0.7),andinstratigraphiccoordinates,theminimumsusceptibilityaxes
(K ) are mainly perpendicular to the bedding and the maximum, whereas the medium axes (K and K )
3 1 2
are scattered within the bedding plane (Figure S3), indicating a normal magnetic fabric of sedimentary
rocks. Stepwise thermal demagnetization of all the samples produced consistent results among the five
sections.Thenaturalremanentmagnetizationintensitiesrangefrom1to20mA/m.Mostsamplesrecorded
two well‐defined components (Figures 2a, 2b, and S4a–S4j). A low‐temperature component removed
below400°Cresemblesthepresentgeomagneticfielddirectioningeographiccoordinates(FigureS5)and
isinterpretedastheviscousremanentmagnetizationsacquiredinthepresentgeomagneticfield.Ahigh‐
temperaturecomponent(HTC)wasidentifiedbetween400°Cand690°C,anditdecayedlinearlytoward
theorigininorthogonalvectordiagrams.Magnetizationsdecayedabruptlytozeroatunblockingtempera-
turesof 660–690 °C (FigureS4k), indicating that the HTCwas carried by hematite, asalso supported by
IRM acquisition curves, backfield demagnetization of IRM, and the Lowrie test (Figure S6 and Text S1),
which revealed the dominance of high‐coercivity and high unblocking temperature magnetic minerals
(Dunlop&Özdemir,1997).
The HTC of the Qishuwan Section has dual‐polarity directions: mostly southwest and down, and minor
northeast and up (Figures 2, S1, and S2a). The magnetic polarity was determined based on the
CarboniferousandyoungerpolesfromtheSCB(Zhangetal.,2015).TheNEupward(SWdownward)direc-
tionsaresuggestedasgeomagneticallynormal(reversal)polarity.TheHTCyieldedasite‐meandirectionof

seven reliability criteria of Van der Voo (1990) (Text S2) and represents a key pole for the SCB in the

PreviouslypublishedDevonianpaleomagneticdatasetsfromEastYunnan(Fangetal.,1989)andGuizhou
(Zhangetal.,2001)areconsistentinlowinclinationandthepresenceofdual‐polaritydirections,butthereis
~50°differenceindeclinationthatcannotbeneglected.Thisdifferenceisprobablyduetoregionalrotation
ofEasternYunnan,whichisboundedbythePanzhihuaandXianshuihe–XiaojiangFaults(Figure1a;Yang
&Besse,1993).OurnewresultsareconsistentwithbutslightlydifferentfromtheEarly–MiddleDevonian
resultsofZhangetal.(2001).TheconsistencyatteststothereliabilityofthosedatafromGuizhou,whereas
theslightdifferenceindirectionsmayhaveresultedfromthedisparityinage.Thus,inthefollowingdiscus-
sions,thepoleofFangetal.(1989)isnotused,whereasthetwopolesofZhangetal.(2001)derivedfromlate
EarlyDevonian–earlyMiddleDevonianandLateDevonian–EarlyCarboniferousstrataaretakenasrefer-
encepolesat~400and~360MafortheSCB,respectively.
4. Paleogeographic Implications
Anewmodelofpaleogeographicevolutionwasobtainedbyfittingtheapparentpolarwanderpaths(APWPs)
betweentheSCBandGondwana(Figure3).TheSCBAPWPwasmainlymodifiedfromZhangetal.(2015),

APWPs suggests that the SCB was connected to East Gondwana from the earliest Cambrian to Early

(Figure3a;Lietal.,2017);and(3)paleontologicalevidencesuggeststheproximityoftheSCBtobothIndia
andAustraliaduringtheEarlyPaleozoic(Figure3d;Metcalfe,2013;Wangetal.,2010).
OurmodelalsopermitsreconstructionsforsomesmallblocksofSEAsiabetweentheSCBandGondwanaas
supported by recently published data (Figure 3a). Based on animal fossil records (Burrett et al., 1990),
tectono‐stratigraphic correlation (Zhu et al., 2013), and provenance analyses (Burrett et al., 2014; Song
et al., 2017; Zhu et al., 2011), Himalaya and South Qiangtang were adjacent to North India, whereas
Lhasa and Sibumasu were located next to NW Australia. The position of Sibumasu outboard NW
Australia and close to Lhasa is also supported by paleomagnetic evidence from the Woniusi basalt (Xu
etal.,2015).IndochinawaslocatedbetweenthewestSCBandSouthQiangtang,basedonthefindingsthat
they share correlatable sedimentological and animal fossil records (Cocks & Torsvik, 2013; Thanh et al.,
1996;Wangetal.,2010),andsimilardetritalzirconagespectra(Usukietal.,2013).
ThedecoupledAPWPsoftheSCBandGondwanasuggestthattheSCBbegantobreakupfromGondwana
after ~400 Ma. The Devonian–Carboniferous segment of the Gondwana APWP displays a great loop,
whereas the Middle Devonian–Permian poles of the SCB show the opposite direction (Figure 3a; Huang
et al., 2008; Wu et al., 1999; Zhang et al., 2001). The Emsian basaltic rocks in the Youjiang Basin of the
southwestSCB(Zhaoetal.,1996)andtheLoeiFoldBeltofNWIndochina(Udchachonetal.,2017)could
representevidenceofinitialrifting(Figures3aand3d).Therift–driftprocessisinferredtohaveoccurred
duringtheEmsian–Givetian,leadingtotheincipientspreadingoftheeasternPaleo‐TethysOceanbetween
theCimmeriancontinent(e.g.,SibumasuandSouthQiangtang)anditsnorthernblocks(e.g.,SouthChina
andIndochina)(Metcalfe,2013).However,weestimatethattheSCBdidnotdriftfarfromGondwanaat
~385Ma,astheirpolesat thistime stillcloselymatched(Figures3a and3b). AftertheGivetian, asEast
Gondwana migrated toward the high‐latitude region, the SCB remained in the equatorial zone, and the
Paleo‐TethysOceanbetweenthemspreadquickly,accompaniedwithenhancedvolcanicactivityandexten-
sivechertdevelopinginthesouthwestSCB(Zhaoetal.,1996)andNESibumasu(Haraetal.,2010).Bythe
endoftheDevonian(Figure3c),theSCBwasseparatedfromEastGondwanabythePaleo‐TethysOcean
whoselatitudinalwidthwas~1,600kmestimatedbasedonthepaleomagneticdata,resultingindramatic
differences in the sedimentary and paleontological records between the SCB and Gondwanan blocks (as
recordedinNESibumasuandAustralia;Haraetal.,2010;Metcalfe,2013).
Between the SCB and Indochina, existing fish fossils suggest their connection until the Mid‐Devonian
(Thanhetal.,1996),whereaslaterophiolitesintheAilaoshan(~383–376Ma)andJinshajiang(~346–341
Ma) sutures indicate the spreading of the Ailaoshan Ocean from the Late Devonian to Early
Carboniferous(Figures3b–3d;Jianetal.,2009).Thesefindings,combinedwiththeLatePermiansubduction
andTriassiccollision(Cai&Zhang,2009),implytheevolutionofacompleteWilsoncyclebetweenthese
twoblocks.
TheseparationprocessesbetweentheSCB,Indochina,andGondwanaarealsoconsistentwithpaleobiogeo-
graphicevidencethatthebioticprovinceoftheSCBandIndochinachangedfromtheGondwananbiotic
province(EarlyDevonian)toatransitionalprovince(Middle–LateDevonian),andthentotheCathaysian
province (Carboniferous–Permian), whereas Sibumasu remained in the Gondwanan province until the
EarlyPermian(Figure3d;Metcalfe,2013).
5. Conclusions
A new paleomagnetic pole of 33.6°N, 236.4°E (A = 3°, N = 34) was obtained from the red beds of the
95
GivetianYuntaiguanFormationinthecentralSCB.ThepolepassesaC‐classreversaltestandafoldtest,
anddiffersfromallyoungerpolesoftheSCB,meetingallsevenofVanderVoo'scriteriaandmanifesting
itsprimaryorigin.Thisnewpaleopole,incombinationwithexistingrobustpoles,locatestheSCBinthe
equatorial region throughout the Paleozoic. Comparison of the Paleozoic APWPs between the SCB and
Gondwana suggests that the SCB was connected to East Gondwana from the earliest Cambrian to Early
Devonian,with itsposition closed to NW Australia. The SCBbegan tobreak up fromGondwanaduring
~400–385 Ma, accompanied with the opening of the Paleo‐Tethys Ocean, but it was not far away from
Gondwana until ~385 Ma. During ~385–360 Ma, as East Gondwana drifted toward the southern polar
region,theSCBremainedintheequatorialzone,andwasseparatedfromGondwanabythePaleo‐Tethys
Oceanwithalatitudinalwidthof~1,600kmby~360Ma.
